witness.summary: The witness is the proof that a run did what it claims: a check the worker never sees fails on the target branch and passes on the PR, and the flip stamps the run. Oxagen has the record half: witnesses and verdicts tables (migration 20260915205000), proof.observed frames on the tacho ingest, get_run_proof, the L0–L3 disclosure grain contract and a proven figure on Spend (ADR-064, issue #2955 open). Nothing executes yet: no witness runner in infra, no witness author, no evaluators, no signed certificate, no verify endpoint, and no Proof tab because the Run page is a stub.

dod.summary: The definition of done locks a set of mechanical checks before an agent starts and refuses to let it finish until they hold, then signs a certificate against the sealed run and records the non-billable dod.held action. Nothing of the runtime DoD exists in oxagen or stella: no packages/dod, no harness hooks, no dod.* contracts, no dod_sets/dod_certificates tables, no Done tab (the Run page is a stub). What exists is the repository-level dod GitHub check that gates pull requests on an issue checklist (ADR-049, dod-check/dod-recheck workflows) and Stella's task-contract DefinitionOfDone type, which the spec names as precedents.

decisions.title: One assembler, two planes, storage stays plural
decisions.question: Should Oxagen unify steering onto a single store (the graph), or keep sources plural and unify only the read path?
decisions.recommendation: Storage stays plural, one writer per fact. What must be single is the assembler: the one function where everything competes for the agent's context. Steering (advisory, ranked, budgeted) and gating (deterministic, never budgeted) stay two planes, authored on one surface and compiled twice.
decisions.decided: Approved in full. assembleSteering(run, budget) returns a stable prefix, a volatile selection and a manifest of what was cut, recorded as a steering.manifest frame.

decisions.title: tachod grows into the gateway
decisions.question: Should Oxagen route model and MCP traffic through a cloud-hosted proxy, a loopback proxy inside the existing tachod daemon, or not build a proxy at all?
decisions.recommendation: A loopback model proxy inside tachod: no extra network hop, prompt bodies never leave the machine, the vendor credential stays on the machine, metering becomes observed for every harness.
decisions.source: ADR-094 (oxagen PR #3294), built in oxagen PR #3319
decisions.decided: Approved and built (#3319 merged 2026-09-18): Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions passthrough on 127.0.0.1 with streaming, one llm_call frame per observed call with cost_basis observed, session_limit_usd refused at the proxy when the bundle's budget mode is enforced, and interrupt delivered as interrupt on the gateway tier. The MCP aggregator is not built (issue #3299 item 6), and enforcement covers only traffic actually routed: a person can unset the base URL.

decisions.title: Sandbox as the top tier, not the only tier
decisions.question: Should every wrapped agent run inside a mandatory OS sandbox, or should containment be one tier among several?
decisions.recommendation: Sandbox is the top tier, aimed at CI, headless runs and managed devices first, never mandatory on a developer's own laptop. Hooks stay. The tier ladder is four words, computed from what was actually routed: observe, harness, gateway, contained.
decisions.decided: Approved. contained is the only tier that earns the word "enforced" against the machine's operator; oxagen run -- <agent> and the witness runner build on the same launcher in Phase 5.

decisions.title: A workspace is born with its main repository
decisions.question: Should create_workspace require a main repository, and how do a second and third repository attach?
decisions.recommendation: A second create_workspace requires owner/name and binds it in one transaction; the org's first workspace stays repo-less and binds through the onboarding banner. Further repositories link and unlink with role linked; the main role is exclusive across the store.
decisions.source: oxagen ADR-099, PR #3326 (open), spec §17 M0; exclusivity index from PR #3269
decisions.decided: ADR-099 rides open PR #3326 with link_repository, unlink_repository, list_repositories, the Repositories section in Workspace settings and oxagen repo list|link|unlink. The exclusive main index (one repository is main for one workspace anywhere) merged in #3269.

decisions.title: Organisation graph placement: pooled by default
decisions.question: Does every organisation get its own Neo4j database, or share one with per-pattern tenant anchors?
decisions.recommendation: Pooled by default with an org anchor on every pattern; a per-org database (CREATE DATABASE org-<ns>) for a dedicated plane; Aura refuses.
decisions.decided: Merged in #3310: OrgGraphProvisioner (pooled | cypher | aura throws), org.data_planes.graph_database, and a real-Neo4j cross-tenant probe in the rls-integration job. Open: workspace-scoped sessions do not refuse Cypher that omits the workspace, the per-org path never ran against Enterprise, and no free-to-dedicated migration exists (#3318).

decisions.title: BYOK to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
decisions.question: Do organisations bring keys only for the named providers, or any endpoint that speaks the OpenAI shape?
decisions.recommendation: Any https endpoint that speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, with a model map; the outbound-URL guard blocks private and metadata addresses.
decisions.decided: Merged in #3290: provider openai_compatible with base_url and model_map on org model credentials, set/get/verify/delete_model_credential on api and mcp, and the SSRF bypass through IPv4-mapped addresses closed. No app UI: the Funding tab remains a gap. Residue: direct-key models lose their provider identity (#3314), structured output assumed (#3324).

decisions.title: The main product: Oxagen as the control plane
decisions.question: How much of Mission Control ships, and on what architecture.
decisions.decided: Oxagen becomes a control plane: a gateway that runs every agent inside a sandbox Oxagen controls. This builds on D24 (sandbox as the top tier) and D23 (the gateway lives in tachod). It is now the main product. Mission Control ships full functionality for every wireframe except the DoD (M3) and the witness protocol (M4), which already sit deprioritized under D15 and D19. Positioning must not read as sandbox infrastructure, the way Modal or E2B are read.
